延.meaning: A runner crosses the finish line in <part>correct</part> form, but the judges keep moving the tape. One more <part>long stride</part>, then another, then another. The race never ends: they <kanji>prolong</kanji> it forever.
延.on: An <sound>en</sound>gine hums along beside him, dragging the finish line further away.
延.kun: '<sound>No</sound>!' gasps the runner, as the tape slides away from him again.

無.meaning: A <part>diving board</part> juts out over a tall frame of <part>pole</part> stilts, and far below there's no pool at all, just <part>hot coals</part>. You walk out to the end and look down. Water? Not a drop. Just <kanji>nothingness</kanji>.
無.on: A <sound>moo</sound>se peers over the edge beside you and shakes its head: nothing down there.
無.kun: You'd happily jump for a puffy <sound>na</sound>an, but there isn't a single one down there.

天.meaning: A <part>large</part> man spreads his arms wide and jumps, and his head bumps a <part>one</part>-plank ceiling far above. Behind it there are stars, clouds and the moon. He has touched the <kanji>heavens</kanji>.
天.on: Up there a <sound>ten</sound>or sings so loudly that the clouds shake.
天.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' sigh the angels, sipping cloud tea from a <sound>mu</sound>g, until one of them sneezes: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

虫.meaning: A little box of a body sits on one tall leg, with a tiny dot of a tail at its foot. It twitches, it buzzes, and it crawls straight up your sleeve. It's an <kanji>insect</kanji>.
虫.on: The insect gets stuck in a blob of <sound>chew</sound>ing gum on the sole of your shoe.
虫.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se sneezes the insect off its nose and onto a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.

風.meaning: An <part>insect</part> hides under a <part>table</part> as a <part>slash</part> of air whips in over the top, flapping the tablecloth like a sail. Napkins fly, and the bug clings on for dear life. It's the <kanji>wind</kanji>.
風.on: The wind blows every scrap of <sound>foo</sound>d off the table and into the hedge.
風.kun: The wind lifts a <sound>ca</sound>rp out of the pond and drops it in a <sound>ze</sound>n garden.

買.meaning: At the market, you drag a <part>net</part> full of <part>shellfish</part> up to the counter. The fishmonger weighs it, names a price, and you hand over your coins. It's yours: you <kanji>buy</kanji> it.
買.on: You strap the dripping net onto your <sound>bi</sound>ke and pedal home.
買.kun: At home, a hungry <sound>ca</sound>rp eyes your shellfish from its bowl.

欠.meaning: A <part>person</part>, <part>wrap</part>ped in a blanket, yawns so wide you can count her teeth. One, two, three… a gap where one is missing. She's missing a good night's sleep too. Everything about her is a <kanji>lack</kanji>.
欠.on: She yawns over a plate of fries, but there's no <sound>ketch</sound>up left in the bottle.
欠.kun: Even her fish bowl lacks something: the <sound>ca</sound>rp has jumped out.

飲.meaning: After all that <part>food</part>, you <part>yawn</part> so wide that your mouth turns into a funnel. Someone pours a whole jug of milk straight in. Glug, glug, gulp. That's how you <kanji>drink</kanji>.
飲.on: Oops: the jug was full of <sound>in</sound>k, and now your teeth are black.
飲.kun: '<sound>No</sound> more!' you gasp, wiping a milk moustache off your lip.

語.meaning: You give a <part>speech</part> in a new language, and every time you get a word right, the crowd gives you a <part>high five</part>. Hello, thanks, cat: slap, slap, slap. You learn it one <kanji>word</kanji> at a time.
語.on: Your teacher writes the new words on the lenses of her swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles.
語.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp in a <sound>tu</sound>b won't stop talking, telling you its whole life story.

明.meaning: The <part>sun</part> and the <part>moon</part> both stay up at once, side by side, and neither will set. No shadows anywhere, no night at all: the sky is <kanji>bright</kanji> around the clock.
明.on: Even the deepest corner of the hedge <sound>ma</sound>ze is lit up.
明.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' you squint, and a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the pond squints back at you.

迷.meaning: You scatter <part>rice</part> grains along a <part>ramp</part> to find your way back, but birds peck them up behind you. Every path looks the same now. You've gone <kanji>astray</kanji>.
迷.on: The path leads you into a hedge <sound>ma</sound>ze, and now you're truly lost.
迷.kun: Lost, you sit down with a <sound>mu</sound>g of tea and a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt and wait to be found.

税.meaning: At harvest a horned <part>imp</part> turns up with a sack and helps himself to every tenth sheaf of <part>grain</part>. 'For the king,' he grins. You can't say no. It's the <kanji>tax</kanji>.
税.on: With each sack he takes, the imp does a <sound>za</sound>ny little dance on your doorstep.

込.meaning: Everyone wants in at once: a whole crowd squeezes up the <part>ramp</part> and through one narrow <part>entrance</part>, elbows out, toes trodden on. Nobody can move an inch. It's <kanji>crowded</kanji>.
込.kun: Somehow a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala squeezes in too, riding on someone's head.

替.meaning: Two men, each a <part>husband</part>, meet at noon in a <part>sun</part>-baked square, each holding the other's hat. On the count of three: swap! Hats on, handshake, done. A fair <kanji>exchange</kanji>.
替.on: Then they swap neckties too: one <sound>tie</sound> striped, one spotted.
替.kun: To finish the deal, they swap a <sound>ca</sound>rp for an <sound>e</sound>gg.

新.meaning: On a little <part>stand</part>, a carpenter props up a <part>tree</part> trunk, picks up his <part>axe</part> and chops. Fresh chips fly, the wood smells sweet, and out comes a chair nobody has ever sat on. Brand <kanji>new</kanji>.
新.on: The first person to try the new chair bangs their <sound>shin</sound> on it.
新.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>! <sound>Tah</sound>-dah! <sound>Rah</sound>-rah!' the carpenter cheers, showing off the new chair.

白.meaning: A sun in a box, with one spark flying off the top. It glows so hot that every colour in the room burns away, and when you look at it you see nothing but <kanji>white</kanji>.
白.on: A <sound>huck</sound>leberry dropped in the snow is the only thing that isn't white.
白.kun: A knight paints his <sound>shi</sound>eld white, then a <sound>ro</sound>dent scampers across it with muddy paws.

糸.meaning: A <part>twist</part> of fluff is spun tighter and tighter on top, and three <part>little</part> strands dangle loose underneath. Pull one and it keeps coming, thin and endless: <kanji>thread</kanji>.
糸.on: A knight sews a torn strap back onto his <sound>shi</sound>eld with it.
糸.kun: An <sound>ee</sound>l winds itself round a <sound>to</sound>tem pole like thread on a spool.

線.meaning: A <part>thread</part> is tied to a stone at the bubbling <part>spring</part>, and you walk off unrolling it behind you, over fields and hills. Look back: one long, thin <kanji>line</kanji> all the way home.
線.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try walks along the thread all night, guarding the line.
線.kun: A <sound>su</sound>shi chef draws a line of soy sauce across the plate, as straight as a <sound>jee</sound>p track.

泊.meaning: <part>water drops</part> patter on a <part>white</part> tent pitched by the lake. You meant to head home at dusk, but it's dark and wet, so you crawl into your sleeping bag. Looks like you're staying <kanji>overnight</kanji>.
泊.on: Supper is <sound>huck</sound>leberry jam on toast, eaten by torchlight in the tent.
泊.kun: You tie the tent to a <sound>to</sound>tem pole so it won't blow away in the night.

宿.meaning: Under one <part>roof</part>, a tired <part>lodger</part> drops his bags, signs the book, and gets a key, a bed and a bowl of soup. One night, then off down the road again. It's an <kanji>inn</kanji>.
宿.on: The innkeeper leaves a <sound>su</sound>gar <sound>cu</sound>be on every pillow.
宿.kun: Every bed in the inn has a blanket of <sound>ya</sound>rn with a <sound>do</sound>lphin knitted on it.

比.meaning: Two spoons stand side by side, both facing the same way. Which one is bigger? Which one is shinier? You hold them up together, turning them in the light, to <kanji>compare</kanji>.
比.on: Next you compare two shoes, measuring each <sound>hee</sound>l with a spoon.
比.kun: Compare a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock with a cheerleader's '<sound>Rah</sound>-rah!': which one is louder?

階.meaning: A <part>pennant</part> flies from the roof of a tall block where <part>all</part> the family lives stacked up: grandparents at the bottom, cousins in the middle, the baby at the top. Each of them has their own <kanji>storey</kanji>.
階.on: From the top storey, the baby flies a <sound>ki</sound>te out of the window.
階.kun: A brass <sound>key</sound> under a ba<sound>za</sound>ar rug opens a little <sound>hu</sound>t at the top of the stairs, full of <sound>shee</sound>p.

段.meaning: Beside a <part>pole</part> with planks nailed across it, each <part>one</part> a step, a <part>maiden</part> curtseys on every rung as she climbs: up, curtsey, up, curtsey. A teacher ticks a box at each. Reach the top and you've passed the <kanji>grade</kanji>.
段.on: Miss a curtsey and you tumble all the way down to the <sound>dun</sound>geon at the bottom.

終.meaning: A grandmother knits by the fire as <part>winter</part> sets in. The <part>thread</part> runs shorter, the scarf grows longer, and the snow piles up. Last loop, snip. The scarf and the year <kanji>finish</kanji> together.
終.on: She uses the very last bit of thread to sew a button onto a giant <sound>shoe</sound>.
終.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>, at last!' she says, and puts her needles down.

点.meaning: A <part>fortune telling</part> lady drips candle wax over <part>hot coals</part> and stares at where it lands. 'A dot here means love, a dot there means money.' Every future is in one tiny <kanji>spot</kanji>.
点.on: A <sound>ten</sound>or bursts in singing, and a drop of wax lands right on the tip of his nose.
点.kun: The smoke makes her sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', which blows out the candle, so she has to light it again.

楽.meaning: On a <part>tree</part> stand sits a big <part>white</part> drum, with two little cymbals of <part>ice</part> tinkling at its sides. Boom, ting, ting! The whole forest starts to dance. It's <kanji>music</kanji>.
楽.on: A <sound>gag</sound>gle of geese honks along to the beat.
楽.kun: '<sound>Tah</sound>-dah!' says the drummer, ready to stop. '<sound>No</sound>, more!' yells the crowd. This is too much fun.

助.meaning: You're carrying one heavy box, and <part>moreover</part> there are ten more stacked in the van. A neighbour flexes a big <part>muscle</part>, grabs the whole pile and carries it all upstairs. Now that's <kanji>help</kanji>.
助.on: A passing <sound>jo</sound>gger stops to lend a hand and carries the lamp.
助.kun: To say thanks, you hand them both a <sound>tu</sound>b of <sound>su</sound>shi.

正.meaning: A learner driver stops exactly on the <part>stop</part> line, with the <part>one</part> bar of the barrier just above the car's nose. Not an inch over. The examiner ticks the box: <kanji>correct</kanji>.
正.on: Her prize, a shiny new licence, has been locked in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe all morning.
正.kun: '<sound>Tah</sound>-<sound>dah</sound>!' she cries, waving her licence out of the window.

曲.meaning: A striker blasts a shot that swerves round the keeper, smacks the <part>goal</part> and drives both posts up through the <part>sun</part> painted on the stadium wall. They stick out crooked forever. That shot had a <kanji>bend</kanji>.
曲.on: The ball curves on into a street <sound>kio</sound>sk and knocks the <sound>cu</sound>ckoo out of its clock.
曲.kun: You bend a spoon stirring a <sound>mu</sound>g of <sound>ga</sound>rlic soup.

角.meaning: A stag hangs the <part>moon</part> on its head like a lantern, a scarf <part>wrap</part>ped over the top and a <part>pole</part> propped underneath to hold it all up. Its antlers jut out every which way, each tip a sharp <kanji>angle</kanji>.
角.on: Far below, wolves circle an old <sound>carc</sound>ass, all ribs and sharp angles.
角.kun: In one corner of the pond, a <sound>ca</sound>rp and a <sound>do</sound>lphin bump noses.
